current.critique: Round 21's pig power as it stands: the light and the runner are one loop the player reads in seconds, and the party going dark when the pig sees a turnip is a clip people would send. What keeps it from the bar is that the dynamo is still pitched as a lumped turn count against brightness, and whether the pig quits rests on scripted temperament. That makes it a slider plus a random interruption, not a machine the player out-thinks.

goals.title: Pig power: the party lasts as long as the friend in the wheel and the machine you built for it
goals.critique: This is round 21's big goal reworded, the fifth treadwheel round in a row, and it scores what it scored. It does answer two faults. Flux from the actual wound path and back-EMF felt in the legs make the winding matter, and a runner on an energy budget makes the pig quitting a consequence of how bright you asked for, not a dice roll. The flywheel fade from white to orange to red is a better moment than a cut to black and real path tracer material. The weak side: the player still mostly sees one number (brightness against minutes), Biot-Savart over every turn is invisible unless the winding visibly makes the light worse, a table of species wattages is a parameter list dressed as friends, and the road is as long as before.

goals.title: Cast a bell; the first strike tells you if you did it right
goals.critique: This is new, and it fits the human's direction squarely. Molten metal, a mould, cooling and a sound computed from the bell's own shape are real materials doing what they do, and hearing the note change live while you draw the profile is a fine minute-to-minute toy. The strike under the tower is a true held-breath bet that ends in either a note or a crack, though a clean ring sounds better in person than in a clip, and the crack is the clip people would send. The weak side: each bell is a long cycle with one verdict at the end, so play leans on drawing the profile. The two hard physics steps, freezing flow that leaves a void and thermal stress that cracks, are exactly what will get faked with a timer. If the crack is not born from the cooling, the payoff is a lie, as round 19's arch would have been.
